label: Is pool guest of
summary: Whether the character is a guest from the pool who is visiting the given character's court.
details: Unlike `is_foreign_court_guest_of`, a pool guest has no liege. Write the host character, whose court is visited, as the value, for example `scope:host`.

label: Is potential knight
summary: Whether the character could become a knight of their liege.
details: The game's documentation says "potential", so it asks about the possibility, not whether they already are a knight. The game's documentation does not list the requirements. Vanilla only uses it with `yes`.

label: Is powerful house
summary: Whether the dynasty house counts as powerful.
details: Works on a dynasty house, for example `scope:house = { is_powerful_family = yes }`. The game's documentation does not say what makes a house powerful.

label: Is powerful vassal
summary: Whether the character is a powerful vassal.
details: The game's documentation does not say what makes a vassal powerful. Use `is_powerful_vassal_of` to check this against one particular liege.

label: Is powerful vassal of
summary: Whether the character is a powerful vassal of the given character.
details: The value is the liege to check against, for example `root` or `liege`. The game's documentation does not say what makes a vassal powerful.

label: Is pregnant
summary: Whether the character is pregnant.

label: Is primary heir of
summary: Whether the character is the heir to the given character's primary title.
details: The value is the character whose heir is checked, for example `root` or `scope:host`.

label: Puppet action possible
summary: Whether the named puppet action could be carried out with any of the puppeteer's puppets.
details: A puppet must be of an active type and the action must pass its own enabled check. The action must be defined as a trigger type, or the game reports an error. Run it on the puppeteer. Vanilla uses it with `puppet_trigger_can_create_rite`.

fields.name: value
fields.values: the key of a puppet action defined as a trigger

label: Is puppet of type
summary: Whether the character is a puppet of the given type under their puppeteer.
details: Run it on the puppet. Vanilla uses it with `theological_agent_puppet`.

fields.name: value
fields.values: the key of a puppet type

label: Is raid army
summary: Whether the army is a raid army.
details: Works on an army. Vanilla only uses it with `yes`.

label: Is being raided
summary: Whether the province is being raided right now.

label: Is raised
summary: Whether the men-at-arms regiment is raised.
details: Works on a men-at-arms regiment.

label: Is regular regiment
summary: Whether the men-at-arms regiment is an ordinary one recruited by a ruler.
details: Works on a men-at-arms regiment. The game's documentation does not name the other kinds it is told apart from. Vanilla does not use it, so nothing beyond the game's documentation is known.

label: Is required special guest
summary: Whether the given character is a required special guest of the activity.
details: Works on an activity. The value is the character to test. Vanilla uses it once, with `prev`.

label: Is rightful liege of
summary: Whether the character is the rightful liege of the given character.
details: The rightful liege of a vassal is the ruler who holds the title that the vassal's primary title belongs to by law (de jure). The game's own text for this key was copied from another check (`was_preferred_heir`) and talks about a preferred heir; vanilla's use settles it: it writes `liege = { is_rightful_liege_of = root }`, and for `scope:recipient = { is_rightful_liege_of = scope:actor }` its tooltip tells the actor that the recipient is their rightful liege.

label: Is rite enabled
summary: Whether the rite is enabled.
details: A rite can be disabled either in its history or by an effect. Write it inside a rite scope, for example `scope:rite = { is_rite_enabled = yes }`.

label: Is river province
summary: Whether the province is a river.
details: The game's documentation treats this as a separate check from `is_riverside_province`.

label: Is riverside county
summary: Whether the county is riverside.
details: Works on a county title. Vanilla only uses it with `yes`. The game's documentation does not say how a county counts as riverside.

label: Is riverside province
summary: Whether the province is riverside.
details: The game's documentation does not say how a province counts as riverside. A river province is checked with `is_river_province`.

label: Ruin being rebuilt
summary: Whether the province has a ruined building that is being reconstructed right now.
details: Only great buildings can be ruined and then rebuilt. Vanilla uses it once, with `no`.

label: Is ruler
summary: Whether the character is a ruler, meaning they hold any title.

label: Is de jure liege or above
summary: Whether the given ruler is the de jure liege of the title, or higher than that.
details: De jure means by the game's title hierarchy, not by who actually holds the lands. Run it on a title and give a character as the value, for example `scope:owner.top_liege`.

label: Is sanctified for faith
summary: Whether the artifact is sanctified for the given faith.
details: Works on an artifact. The value is the faith to test, for example `scope:actor.faith`.

label: Is scheme agent exposed
summary: Whether the given character is an exposed agent in the scheme.
details: Works on a scheme. The value is the character to test.

label: Scheme category
summary: Whether the scheme belongs to the given category.
details: The game's documentation names the categories hostile, contract and personal. Vanilla also uses `political` (15 times), so the documented list may be incomplete.

fields.name: value
fields.values: hostile, contract or personal per the game's documentation; vanilla also uses political

label: Is scheme exposed
summary: Whether the scheme has been exposed.

label: Scheme target type
summary: Whether the scheme's target is of the given type.
details: Vanilla mostly uses `character`.

label: Is scheming against
summary: Whether the character owns, or is an agent in, a scheme aimed at the given target.
details: With only a target, every scheme counts. Add a scheme type to look at one type only. The game's documentation also names a scheme skill filter (`scheme_skill`) that limits it to schemes of one skill category. Vanilla writes that field as `skill`, which does not match the game's documentation.

fields.name: target
fields.text: Who the scheme is aimed at.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Limits the check to schemes of this type.
fields.values: the key of a scheme type, for example murder, seduce or courting

fields.name: scheme_skill
fields.text: Limits the check to schemes of this skill category. Vanilla spells it `skill`.

label: Is sea province
summary: Whether the province is a sea province.

label: Is set
summary: Whether the given scope target has been set.
details: A target that was set to the null object also counts as set. The value is a scope chain, for example `from.owner.var:cool_var.mother`.

label: Is shunned for
summary: Whether the secret is shunned for the given character taking part in it.
details: Works on a secret. The value is the participant to check. Vanilla often passes `secret_owner`.

label: Is shunned or criminal for
summary: Whether the secret is shunned or criminal for the given character taking part in it.
details: Works on a secret. The value is the participant to check. The documented usage line names a different key (`is_shunned_or_illegal_for`), which looks like a typo.

label: Is sibling of
summary: Whether the character is a sibling of the given character.
details: The game's documentation does not say whether half-siblings count.

label: Is situation unique
summary: Whether the type of the situation is unique.
details: Works on a situation. Vanilla does not use it, and the game's documentation does not say what unique means here.

label: Is special guest
summary: Whether the given character is a special guest of the activity, optionally for one type only.
details: Works on an activity. Write a character alone, or a block with a target and a type.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Limits the check to one special guest type.
fields.values: the key of a special guest type

label: Is spent by
summary: Whether the given character has spent the secret.
details: Works on a secret. The value is the character to test.

label: Is spouse of
summary: Whether the character is married to the given character, with both of them alive.
details: If one of them is dead, it is false. See `is_spouse_of_even_if_dead` to count dead spouses.

label: Is spouse of, even if dead
summary: Whether the character is a spouse of the given character, even if one or both have died.
details: This differs from `is_spouse_of`, which needs both to be alive.

label: Is struggle phase
summary: Whether the struggle is currently in the given phase.
details: Works on a struggle. Vanilla uses phases of the Iberian and Persian struggles, for example `struggle_iberia_phase_hostility`.

fields.name: value
fields.values: the key of a struggle phase

label: Is struggle type
summary: Whether the struggle is of the given type.
details: Works on a struggle. Vanilla uses `iberian_struggle` and `persian_struggle`.

fields.name: value
fields.values: the key of a struggle type
